besluite.fout: 'die rede hou nie' copies English 'does not hold'; the Afrikaans idiom is 'hou nie steek nie', and the two clauses lack the AWS comma before 'en'.
besluite.rede: Restores the fixed expression and adds the required AWS comma without changing what the sentence says.
'Hy sal die klas ophou' is natural, plain Afrikaans for holding the class up, so 'vertraag' is a lateral and slightly more formal swap.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb ('Die lyn is ... oop' / 'iemand luister').
besluite.rede: Punctuation only; the wording of the instruction is unchanged.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb ('Jou werk is' / 'die grootmense se werk is').
besluite.rede: Punctuation only; the protected word 'vertel' stays intact.

besluite.fout: 'iets wat mense saam doen' is a loose fit for a plan, where Afrikaans says 'n plan maak'.
besluite.rede: 'Maak' narrows the definition from carrying the plan out together to drawing it up, so the writer should choose the verb that says what the lesson means.

besluite.fout: 'sien ... raak' without an object makes a reader stumble and can read as an instruction to notice the class.
besluite.rede: Adding 'dit' makes the class clearly the subject who notices the violation, with no change in meaning.

besluite.fout: 'vertel' takes 'vir' for the person told; 'by wie' is the wrong preposition.
besluite.rede: Grammar fix only: in both versions the plan names the person they will tell, so who is told does not change.
